lastCompletedStory.title: Feed coverage and skip-ratchet from the shared blob in-process

nextStoryContext: scripts/check-all.ts's GATES manifest now has 'coverage' and 'skip-ratchet' as in-process gates: each is a `Gate` object with a `run: (suiteOutput: string, cwd: string) => { ok: boolean; errors: string[] }` field instead of `cmd`/`args`. `Gate` is one flat interface with cmd/args/run all optional (NOT a discriminated union -- see the patterns.md bullet on why: a real union broke every pre-existing `gate?.cmd` test assertion via TS narrowing). `isInProcessGate`/`isSpawnGate` are the runtime guards; `executeGate` dispatches; `runSpawnGate`/`runInProcessGate` do the actual work; `reportGateOutcome` prints/records. The shared suite blob (captured by the 'test' gate, per US-001) is threaded through a local `suiteOutput` variable in `runGates`'s loop, updated only when a spawn gate named 'test' runs, then passed to every later in-process gate's `run` call. Both in-process gates call `checkCoverage`/`checkSkipRatchet` with ONLY `getCoverage`/`getSuiteOutput` overridden (never `getStagedDiff`/`readExpectations`), so the coverage budget's tracker-ref check and the real lane-expectations file both stay live in the collapsed path. `bun run check:all` now costs exactly ONE `bun test --coverage` run for the whole 14-gate spine (measured: 103.3s single run, confirmed via `grep -c '^ok test ('` on a full check:all invocation). US-003 (per the CAM-488 PRD, if it exists) should verify the two consumer scripts (check-coverage.ts, check-skip-ratchet.ts) still run standalone correctly on their own -- their `makeDefaultGetCoverage`/`makeDefaultGetSuiteOutput` adapters were left completely untouched by this story, only check-all.ts's manifest and runner changed.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure internal wiring: reuses checkCoverage/checkSkipRatchet and their existing production adapters (already validated in prior stories); no new external library surface introduced.
